observations: body L1: the head of the notes on chapter 8, «Ad» and «caput» in small capitals, in the larger type of the heads.

body L6, L10, L14: the dashes of «al-Battānī» and «al–Battānī» measure 3.0 pt in L6, 4.7 pt in L10 and 3.7 pt in L14 (the long dashes of the name elsewhere about 5.4 pt); transcribed as a hyphen, a long dash and a hyphen.
body L19: the dash of «69-70» measures 4.1 pt and stands free of the figures, as a hyphen; transcribed so.
body L11: the bar of the fraction is printed broken.
body L12: the hyphen of «aequi-» printed only as a dot.
body L15-L17, L29: the minus signs of the formulas and of «90° − P pro P − 90°» are printed as long dashes; they are set as minus signs.
body L17: the R before the note number is printed in the other italic form, with an open bowl.

body L18-L23: the figure of p. 177 is printed again from the same block, at the left of lines 18 to 23, which are set beside it in a narrow measure; it is redrawn from measurements of this print in the same way (the meridian ABGD, the equator AEG, the horizon BED and the circle of declination PTHZ; the dashed line PEZ; the bold italic letters).
body L23: the first numerator and the middle denominator are set close, without spaces, as printed.

body L11, L15-L29: the formulas are checked. With the distance from the north point HD = 90° + HE, sin HD = cos ampl. solst., and rule (α) is that of the note a) on chapter 7; rule (β) with HE = ampl. solst. gives L17. Menelaus' theorem in L21 with ET = 90° − P, AT = P, EH = ampl. solst., HB = 90° − ampl. solst., BZ = φ and ZA = 90° gives L23, L25 and L27; Ptolemy's 90° − P for P − 90° accounts for the sign (L28-L29). Note 1: with the two substitutions the rule becomes tg φ = − cos P cotg ε for the radius 1.
